meta.title: Japanese — Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 292 set phrases and grammatical chunks — alongside any level
meta.desc: The set phrases a learner needs beside the vocabulary: greetings and courtesies (お願いします, お邪魔します), and the fixed chunks Japanese grammar is built from (かもしれない, ことができる). 292 phrases, each ONE note with TWO cards (Japanese → English, English → Japanese), each scheduled on its own. THE SELECTION: every expression JMdict marks as common that is not already carded in the five JLPT decks and that the Tatoeba corpus uses in at least 3 sentences, commonest first — less the ones made only of particles and auxiliaries (には, だった), which are grammar points rather than phrases. The card is the vocabulary decks' card: the phrase as it is written (in kana where the dictionary marks it usually kana), furigana and Hepburn romaji (a particle は written "wa", へ "e", を "o"), the meanings, and up to three real sentences with furigana and a speaker. — Phrases, readings and meanings: JMdict (Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, CC BY-SA 4.0). Furigana: JmdictFurigana (CC BY-SA 4.0). Kanji: KANJIDIC2 (EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0) and KanjiVG (CC BY-SA 3.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR; the readings over them come from segmenting the corpus with MeCab and UniDic, so a reading over an example sentence is a machine's and can occasionally be wrong — the headword's own reading is the dictionary's.
